title: WhereToBuild
publisher: Warwick CAGE (Datta & Kulka), built on 20bn Rightmove searches + listings 2019-2024
temporalGrain: One-off pooled snapshot (search/listing data pooled across 2019-2024, not a time series)
access: Interactive map only - no visible bulk-download link; underlying data needs a request to the research team
goodFor: The headline "demand outstrips supply 5:1" framing; a ready-made proxy for where housing is wanted, not just where it's built
caveats: It's search/listing-based demand, not need - skews toward people who can already afford to search on Rightmove

title: ONS Census 2021
access: Nomis / ONS website, CSV
goodFor: Household composition, overcrowding, tenure mix, dwelling counts - the "need" side of the equation
caveats: Getting stale by the time #1/#2 run; 2031 Census is a long way off

title: English Indices of Deprivation 2025
spatialGrain: LSOA (33,755 areas), summarised to local authority / ward
temporalGrain: Point-in-time relative ranking (released 30 Oct 2025, methodology changed from 2019 - not directly time-comparable)
access: Bulk CSV via the Local Deprivation Explorer, or postcode/LSOA lookup tool
goodFor: Brand new release, still under a year old. One of the seven domains, "Barriers to Housing and Services," is directly relevant; also useful as general socioeconomic context alongside Census for the "need" side of Brief 1/5
caveats: Relative ranking only, not an absolute measure - a low-deprivation-rank area isn't necessarily "fine," just less deprived than elsewhere in England; don't compare scores directly against the 2019 release

title: Housing in London (annual report)
access: PDF + data tables on London Datastore
goodFor: Headline stats and links to the underlying spreadsheets in one place - good starting point for context, not raw data
caveats: It's a report, not a clean dataset - expect PDF tables

title: Residential starts / completions / pipeline dashboards (Planning London Datahub)
access: Power BI dashboards on data.london.gov.uk; bulk download not currently possible from the dashboard itself
goodFor: Tracking the gap between permissions granted and homes actually delivered
caveats: GLA flags this data as not quality-checked - self-reported by boroughs/applicants, expect gaps and errors

title: London Development Database (LDD) export
temporalGrain: Historical archive, extract taken July 2020 (one-off, not current)
access: SQL dump (~160MB, pg_dump) on London Datastore
updateFrequency: Historical snapshot, one-off (superseded by the Datahub above)
goodFor: The richest scheme-level history if you want site-level detail rather than aggregates
caveats: It's an archived export from 2020, not live - needs a Postgres restore to query

title: Affordable Housing Open Data
access: London Datastore, XLSX
goodFor: Tracking the affordable homes share of delivery against London Housing Strategy targets, up to 2021
caveats: GLA flags this dataset does not incorporate DLUHC 2021/22 or GLA 2022/23 data - check whether a newer source is needed

title: GLA Affordable Housing Programme Outturn
access: London Datastore, XLSX/PDF
goodFor: Starts/completions specifically for GLA-funded affordable programmes, actively maintained
caveats: Only covers GLA-funded schemes - a slice of total supply, not all of it

title: EPCs for new dwellings
publisher: MHCLG (Get energy performance of buildings data service)
access: Bulk CSV or developer API - now requires a free GOV.UK One Login account
goodFor: Genuinely one of the more reliable new-build completion proxies - MHCLG itself points to this over building-control stats
caveats: The old open epc.opendatacommunities.org site was retired 30 May 2026; the replacement needs sign-in, which is a real step to build into a hackathon workflow - worth setting up an account in advance

title: MHCLG "indicators of new supply" (building control)
access: Quarterly statistical release + live tables, GOV.UK
goodFor: Independent cross-check against GLA figures
caveats: Gross not net, no conversions/acquisitions, known undercount

title: Housing Delivery Test
access: ODS/PDF release, GOV.UK
goodFor: The most direct dataset for the "London isn't on track to hit its target" framing - a single %-delivered-vs-required figure per borough, with statutory consequences below 95%/85%/75% thresholds
caveats: Publication has fallen behind schedule - the latest measurement (2023) was only published Dec 2024, so treat as lagging rather than current

title: Planning Data API (planning.data.gov.uk)
temporalGrain: Varies by dataset - most have per-entity start-dates, rolling
access: REST API, OpenAPI spec, bulk downloads (CSV/JSON/GeoJSON/Parquet), interactive map
goodFor: 100+ datasets in one consistent schema: planning applications, conservation areas, listed buildings, green belt, article 4 directions, brownfield land, flood risk - the single best entry point for planning-constraint data
caveats: Coverage varies a lot by local authority - absence of a record does not equal absence of the constraint

title: Digital Planning Register / individual borough registers
publisher: Boroughs on PlanX/BOPS (18+ councils incl. Lambeth, Southwark, Camden)
temporalGrain: Per-application, rolling (full lifecycle from submission to decision)
access: Varies - some via Open Digital Planning schema (JSON), many still borough-by-borough HTML search forms
goodFor: The actual application text, decision (approve/refuse), and officer reasoning - what you'd need to train a decision classifier
caveats: No single London-wide feed; scraping/normalising ~33 borough portals is real work in itself

title: UK PlanIt
publisher: Independent, one-person project (Andrew Speakman) - scrapes ~420 UK planning authority portals into one database
temporalGrain: Per-application, rolling; historical coverage generally back to 2000-2002 depending on authority
access: Free JSON/CSV API (rate-limited to ~1 request/minute on the applics endpoint), no key or attribution required, plus a searchable web UI
updateFrequency: Rolling, updated as each authority is re-scraped
goodFor: Solves the exact "no single London-wide feed" problem above - one API call across all London boroughs instead of ~33 separate scrapes; supports spatial (rectangle/circle/postcode/area) and description text search
caveats: Run solo as a "retirement hobby," best-effort only, no SLA; full bulk dataset isn't offered (legal caution around scraped council data); no applicant/agent names (data protection); ~9% of applications have no location at all

title: London Plan Opportunity Areas
temporalGrain: Point-in-time designation (current London Plan), reviewed periodically
access: GeoPackage/GIS download on London Datastore
updateFrequency: Periodic, tied to London Plan revisions
goodFor: GLA's own designated growth-capacity areas (typically 5,000+ jobs and/or 2,500+ homes each) - the supply-side counterpart to WhereToBuild's demand mapping; pairs well with the Planning Data API's constraint layers
caveats: These are policy designations, not guarantees - an Opportunity Area being on the map doesn't mean sites within it have permission or are being built out

title: Live tables on planning application statistics
access: GOV.UK, CSV/ODS + Power BI dashboard
goodFor: Decision volumes, approval rates, timeliness (P152/P154) by LPA and nationally - good for benchmarking committees against each other
caveats: Aggregate counts only, not case-level - can't join to specific applications

title: Digital Planning Data Schemas
access: GitHub (JSON Schema), actively maintained (v0.7.7 as of Feb 2026)
goodFor: If a team wants to build/consume PlanX-shaped data, this is the canonical schema
caveats: It's a spec, not a dataset - only useful alongside real application data

title: Price Paid Data
access: Bulk CSV/TXT (1995-present, full or by year) or linked-data API
goodFor: Transaction prices, dates, addresses - the standard source for house-price analysis
caveats: No property size/attributes by default (see EPC-linking note below); excludes some transaction types (e.g. not-at-full-value); Chrome has a known issue blocking the direct download links

title: UK House Price Index
access: GOV.UK, CSV, monthly release
goodFor: Clean, official trend series if a team just needs a price index rather than raw transactions
caveats: Aggregated - not useful for site-level work

title: Domestic EPC register
publisher: MHCLG (Get energy performance of buildings data service)
access: Bulk CSV or API - GOV.UK One Login required
goodFor: Floor area, energy rating, property age/type - the standard way to add size/attributes to Price Paid transactions (published linkage methodology exists, ~90%+ match rates)
caveats: Same site-migration caveat as above - old open-access URL is dead

title: House Price per Square Metre (Price Paid x EPC, pre-linked)
publisher: GLA / academic linkage (UCL, published via London Datastore)
access: Ready-made linked extract on London Datastore - avoids doing the Price Paid/EPC join yourself
goodFor: Skips the linkage work entirely if a team wants price-per-sqm without touching the raw EPC/Price Paid join
caveats: Worth flagging to teams as the shortcut - many will not know it exists and will otherwise try to redo the linkage from scratch

title: Vacant dwellings / long-term empty homes (Live Table 615)
publisher: MHCLG, sourced from local authority Council Tax records
temporalGrain: Annual snapshot at 31 March, series from 2004
access: Bulk XLS/ODS on GOV.UK
goodFor: Directly operationalises the "clear empty homes" policy option - London-specific figures show empty homes up 81% since 2016 (105,138 in 2025)
caveats: Only captures homes classed empty for Council Tax purposes - narrower than genuinely under-used or intermittently-occupied stock; excludes homes with a Council Tax exemption from the headline "empty" count in some tables

title: Overseas / UK companies that own property (OCOD / CCOD)
temporalGrain: Per-registration, monthly complete + change-only files, back to Oct 2015
access: Free CSV/API - requires a free account and agreeing to a data licence
goodFor: The one dataset that lets a team actually quantify the "foreign high-net-worth ownership" policy option (~250k overseas-owned titles) rather than just assert it - includes country of incorporation
caveats: Only covers corporate owners, not private individuals (excluded for data protection); doesn't tell you who owns the company, just its name and incorporation country - beneficial ownership needs linking to Companies House / the Register of Overseas Entities

title: Brownfield land registers
temporalGrain: Point-in-time register entries, refreshed as LPAs re-publish (statutory annual duty)
access: CSV/JSON/GeoJSON/Parquet bulk download
updateFrequency: Rolling, 354 data providers as of July 2026
goodFor: Directly relevant to the "end land banking" and site-viability threads in the problem brief
caveats: Explicitly flagged as incomplete/not covering all of England yet

title: ONS geography lookups (LSOA/MSOA/ward/borough)
temporalGrain: Point-in-time boundary vintage (e.g. 2021 boundaries), periodically revised
access: Shapefile/GeoJSON, free
goodFor: Needed to join any of the above across geographies

title: Local Planning Authority boundaries
access: CSV/JSON/GeoJSON
goodFor: Needed to map borough-level planning data

title: OS Open Data (roads, boundaries, greenspace)
temporalGrain: Periodic OS releases, varies by product
access: Free tier via OS Data Hub (JS-only site, needs a free account)
goodFor: Fine for open-data-tier use; full MasterMap needs a PSMA licence - flag this if a team wants building-level polygons
